title: [Feature]:  conv3d_implicit — accept and emit NDHWC so chained convs skip the layout round-trip
body:
### Suggestion Description

## Ask

`conv3d_implicit` takes NCDHW and calls `_ncdhw_to_ndhwc` on every invocation (L705). In a network that is a *chain* of 3D convolutions, every intermediate could have stayed in NDHWC. Please add a layout parameter so a caller can convert twice per network instead of twice per layer:

```python
conv3d_implicit(
    x, weight, bias=None, stride=1, padding=0,
    layout="NCDHW",        # "NCDHW" (default, unchanged) | "NDHWC"
    out_layout=None,       # None -> same as `layout`
    **kwargs,
)
```

`layout="NDHWC"` skips the input transpose; `out_layout="NDHWC"` lets the non-split-K epilogue write `(n, do, ho, wo, k)`, which is a change of output view rather than new kernel work.

## Why

On a Wan 3D causal VAE encoder (bf16, input `(1, 3, 33, 352, 640)`, 278 conv calls, MI350X / gfx950 / ROCm 7.1.1), layout movement is **17.4% of the 193 ms encoder** — 992 `batched_transpose` kernels, 33.6 ms. Swapping MIOpen for `conv3d_implicit` already removes the weight and output round-trips (`_prep_weight` caches, the `splitk==1` epilogue writes NCDHW), and is **1.20x faster overall** on these shapes: 108.2 → 89.9 ms measured per-shape. What remains is the per-call input transpose, roughly 20 ms that nothing in the network needs.

The dominant shapes are rank-5 `in=[1,96,6,354,642] w=[96,96,3,3,3]`, `in=[1,384,3,46,82] w=[384,384,3,3,3]` and rank-4 `in=[4,96,353,641] w=[96,96,3,3]`, all bf16. Happy to test a branch on them.

## Related

- #861 `[Issue]: Tune conv perf` — tuning the conv itself; this request is about the data movement around it.

### Operating System

_No response_

### GPU

_No response_

### ROCm Component

_No response_

comments.author: jhinpan
comments.body:
## A second consumer for this: MiniMax H3 (Hailuo 3.0)

`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` (open weights, Aug 2026) ships a visual VAE whose encoder is exactly this pattern — a causal 3D CNN consuming NCDHW. A `layout` parameter would apply there too, but the shapes are far enough from the Wan ones above that tuning for Wan alone won't cover it. Details below in case they help scope the change.

Paths below are `Ref2VA/video_vae/...`; the repo ships the VAE once per checkpoint and `FL2VA/video_vae/` is an identical copy.

### The call site is already a clean drop-in

`Ref2VA/video_vae/conv.py` does its own padding and calls `F.conv3d` with `padding=0`:

```python
class BaseConv3d(nn.Conv3d):
    def forward(self, x):
        if sum(self.padding) == 0:
            return super().forward(x)
        x = self._apply_padding(x)   # spatial reflect pad + temporal causal pad
        return F.conv3d(x, self.weight, self.bias,
                        stride=self.stride, padding=0, dilation=self.dilation)
```

Every conv in the encoder is constructed as `SpatialParallelConv3d`, which inherits this `forward` unchanged and only overrides `_apply_padding`. Spatial padding is `reflect`, temporal is causal single-sided zero pad, both applied before the conv — so nothing here depends on `conv3d_implicit`'s own padding handling. (The 1x1x1 convs take the `sum(self.padding) == 0` branch into `nn.Conv3d.forward` instead, but they are negligible FLOPs.)

### Shapes

From `Ref2VA/video_vae/source/config.json`: `ch=128`, `ch_mult=[1,2,2,4,4,8]`, `num_res_blocks=2`, `space_down=[2,2,2,2,1,1]`, `time_down=[1,2,2,1,1,1]`, `use_3d_conv=true`, `causal_encoder=true`. Tiling is configured one level up, in `Ref2VA/video_vae/config.json`: `vae_encoder_tiling=1`, `vae_tile_size=256`, `vae_tile_overlap_min=64`, `vae_clip_length=17`. `stack_tiling` is absent from both files and defaults to `False`, so every tile runs at N=1.

30 3x3x3 conv3d calls per tile per 17-frame clip, bf16:

| stage | shape | count |
|---|---|---|
| conv_in | `in=[1,3,17,256,256] w=[128,3,3,3,3]` | 1 |
| L0 | `in=[1,128,17,256,256] w=[128,128,3,3,3]` | 4, + 1 at stride (1,2,2) |
| L1 | `in=[1,128,17,128,128] w=[256,128,3,3,3]` then `in=[1,256,17,128,128] w=[256,256,3,3,3]` | 1 + 3, + 1 at stride (2,2,2) |
| L2 | `in=[1,256,9,64,64] w=[256,256,3,3,3]` | 4, + 1 at stride (2,2,2) |
| L3 | `in=[1,256,5,32,32] w=[512,256,3,3,3]` then `in=[1,512,5,32,32] w=[512,512,3,3,3]` | 1 + 3, + 1 at stride (1,2,2) |
| L4 | `in=[1,512,5,16,16] w=[512,512,3,3,3]` | 4 |
| L5 | `in=[1,512,5,16,16] w=[1024,512,3,3,3]` then `in=[1,1024,5,16,16] w=[1024,1024,3,3,3]` | 1 + 3 |
| conv_out | `in=[1,1024,5,16,16] w=[48,1024,3,3,3]` | 1 |

Plus three 1x1x1 `nin_shortcut` convs and the 1x1x1 `quant_conv`.

FLOPs concentrate in L0 (~1 TFLOP per conv). L4/L5 are the opposite regime — 16x16 spatial with 512/1024 channels. Neither overlaps much with the `w=[96,96,3,3,3]` / `w=[384,384,3,3,3]` shapes being tuned in #861.

Call volume is higher than the Wan profile because of the 256-tile decomposition. Note that `split_tiles` starts at `ceil(input_len / tile_size)` and then increments until tiles minus overlaps actually cover the input, so 768 lands on 4 tiles and 1376 on 7, not 3 and 6. A 5 s 768x1376 reference clip is 120 frames at 24 fps, snapped up to the next `17n + 5` = 124 — so 4x7 = 28 spatial tiles and 8 temporal chunks (7 full plus one of 5). Roughly 30 x 28 x 8 = 6.7k conv3d calls at N=1, against 278 for the Wan encoder above. Same per-call input transpose, ~24x the count.

### An extra argument for NDHWC that isn't in the original ask

This encoder is not a pure chain of convs — every pair is separated by a GroupNorm, and the config sets `use_t_isolated_gn=true`, so `Ref2VA/video_vae/norm.py` runs a time-to-batch reshape on the way in:

```python
def _merge_time_to_batch(x):        # N,C,D,H,W -> N*D,C,1,H,W
    batch, channels, depth, height, width = x.shape
    return x.permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).contiguous().view(batch * depth, channels, 1, height, width)
```

and permutes back on the way out, where `_split_time_from_batch` is `.contiguous()` as well. With 12 ResnetBlock3D x 2 norms plus `norm_out` = 25 norms, that is 50 full-tensor copies per encoder forward, on top of the conv layout transposes.

**Worth stressing: these copies survive the fusion H3 already ships.** `norm.py` has an opt-in `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM=true` path that swaps in `FusedGroupNorm3D` to fuse the GroupNorm with its SiLU — and that path still calls `_merge_time_to_batch` on the way in and `_split_time_from_batch` on the way out. So these 50 copies are not something kernel fusion can reach on this network; only a layout change can.

This cuts both ways:

- **Against the ask as filed.** Adding `layout` to `conv3d_implicit` alone does not let intermediates stay in NDHWC here. The norm wants C at dim 1, so the transpose just relocates from the conv into the norm.
- **For a stronger version of the ask.** In NDHWC, `_merge_time_to_batch` becomes a pure view: D is already adjacent to N, so `(N,D,H,W,C) -> (N*D,H,W,C)` is free, and all 50 copies disappear. What that needs is a channels-last GroupNorm — and in NDHWC a group's `C/32` channels are contiguous at each spatial position, so the reduction is memory-friendly rather than strided.

So on this network the end-to-end win requires conv and norm to move together. It may be worth saying that explicitly in the API contract: `out_layout="NDHWC"` pays off only when the caller has channels-last versions of whatever sits between the convs.

### Scope caveats

Three things bound how much of H3 this touches:

- **The decoder is not a CNN.** H3 uses `ViT3DDecoder` (36 layers), so the decode path gets nothing from this. Unlike Wan, conv3d exists only on the encode side.
- **The encoder only runs when there is visual input to encode.** Pure `t2va` never calls it. `fl2va` calls it on 1–2 frames (D=1). `ref2va` — up to 9 reference images and 3 reference video clips — is the path that produces the profile above.
- **Spatial parallelism interacts with the layout choice.** The profile above is single-GPU (`vae_encoder_parallel=0`). With it enabled, `SpatialParallelConv3d._apply_padding` exchanges halos across ranks along `vae_chunk_dim=-1`, i.e. W. In NDHWC, W is no longer the innermost dimension, so the exchanged borders stop being contiguous. Worth deciding up front whether `layout` is meant to compose with spatial parallelism or is single-rank only.

Happy to profile the H3 encoder on MI350X the same way if a branch lands.

comments.author: jiacao-amd
comments.body:
Thanks both — this is well-scoped and the profiles help a lot.

I'm on board with adding the layout parameter. A few notes from the kernel side on what's cheap vs. what needs real work:

**Input side (`layout="NDHWC"`)** — trivial, it's just skipping the `_ncdhw_to_ndhwc` call. No kernel change.

**Output side (`out_layout="NDHWC"`)** — splits in two:

  - **split-K path**: already free. The kernel materializes `(npq, k)`, which is NDHWC-flat, then does `.view(n,do,ho,wo,k).permute(0,4,1,2,3)` at the end. So `out_layout="NDHWC"` there is deleting a permute. @ZJLi2013 is right that it's a view change, not new work.
  - **`splitk==1` path**: needs a real epilogue change. It allocates `(n,k,do,ho,wo)` and scatters into it, so NDHWC means recomputing the store offset. Modest work, and it should end up *faster* — the store becomes contiguous along k instead of strided.

  **On the GroupNorm point (@jhinpan)** — good catch, agreed. Conv-only won't get you there on H3, since the transpose just moves into the norm. If GroupNorm goes channels-last too, this gets much better.

  **On spatial parallelism**  —  hadn't thought about that, thanks. You're right that NDHWC breaks the contiguous halo along W. I'd lean toward single-rank only for a first cut.
